This page logs dated minutes from the team's weekly meetings with the faculty advisor during the Senior Design build semester. Select a meeting to expand its minutes.

<Accordion title="Week 12 — 11/09/2026" subtitle="Failed relay, report structure, project priorities">

**Location:** Zoom, 5:00 PM
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Weekly progress check-in and guidance on the structure of the report draft.

**1. Failed relay**

- The team reported that the relay connecting the 24 V power supply to the motor drivers had failed: its normally-open contact stays closed, so the drivers remain powered even when the relay's coil is unpowered by the emergency stop.
- Resolution: the relay is simply replaced. The team attributes the failure to a defective component, not to a defective design, since everything else is within its specifications.

**2. Structure of the report**

- The team and Dr. Socarras discussed the difference between the implementation, the troubleshooting, and the requirements testing and results.
- As examples of what the troubleshooting section could cover, the team proposed the limit-switch bug, the broken ball-bearing housing (on both sides), the tension of the belt, and the heating of the electromagnet. These were also the team's biggest issues with the project, which it raised with Dr. Socarras.
- The electrical schematic goes in Appendix E.

**3. Project priorities**

- The team asked whether it should build the whole control panel to make the project look polished, or focus on the movements of the gantry, the Modbus output and the limit switches.
- Dr. Socarras advised the latter: make it work before making it nice.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Week 11 — 11/02/2026" subtitle="Progress check-in and reflections on the Senior Design experience">

**Location:** Zoom, 5:00 PM
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Weekly progress check-in.

**1. Progress update**

- The team reviewed its progress since the previous meeting.
- Dr. Socarras said she was pleased with the team's progress.

**2. Reflections on Senior Design**

- As the course nears its end, the team and Dr. Socarras discussed how the team feels about the Senior Design Proposal and Senior Design experience as a whole.
- The team noted that, over the course of the project, its two members had taken on many roles beyond engineering: technicians, project managers, technical writers, quality assurance, testers, and purchasing, sourcing and receiving the parts.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Week 10 — 10/26/2026" subtitle="Checkpoint 2 viability video, part-detection sensor replaced by a part-ready trigger">

**Location:** Zoom, 5:00 PM
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Weekly progress check-in following the Checkpoint 2 deadline.

**1. Checkpoint 2 viability video**

- The team thanked Dr. Socarras for extending the deadline of the viability video to Wednesday, October 28.
- The team reported that the system had been built and had been seen working, and that the formal viability video would be submitted later in the week.
- Resolution: the video was posted on the Final Testing & Results page on Tuesday, October 27.

**2. Part-detection sensor (follow-up by email)**

- In an email exchange later that week, the team noted that industry reviewers had questioned the need for a part-detection sensor when the conveyor is outside the project scope, since the sensor's type and position depend on the conveyor used. The team proposed replacing the sensor with a 5 V-tolerant part-ready trigger input, leaving part detection to the external system that supplies the conveyor.
- Dr. Socarras approved the proposal: the sensor is dropped in favor of the trigger input, part detection becomes the responsibility of the external system, and a push button may start the cycle for the demonstration.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Week 8 — 10/12/2026" subtitle="Advisor's follow-up on the emergency stop and fuses, and the team's progress update">

**Location:** Zoom, 5:00 PM
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Receive the advisor's follow-up on the emergency stop and the fuses, and review the team's progress.

**1. Emergency Stop and Fuses**

- Following the question raised at the 10/06 meeting about the emergency stop, Dr. Socarras returned to the team with a possible solution for the fuses and the E-stop.
- The solution is not directly applicable as presented, but it is a good reference for how to handle DC arcing when the E-stop interrupts a DC load.
- The team will use it as a reference when resolving the E-stop and fuse design.

**2. Progress Update**

- The team gave Dr. Socarras its regular update on the progress of the project, and the meeting also included informal conversation.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Week 7 — 10/06/2026" subtitle="Power budget correction, motor supply voltage, website review, e-stop placement, and project priorities">

**Location:** Zoom, 3:00 PM (one hour)
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Review the proposal, the website, and the electrical schematic, and confirm the project's priorities.

**1. Proposal Correction**

- Dr. Socarras identified an error in the proposal, in both the website and the report: the power budget lists the electromagnet as a 24 V load, whereas every other part of the proposal specifies 12 V. The correct value is 12 V.
- Resolution: the team will correct the report.

**2. Motor Supply Voltage**

- The team discussed with Dr. Socarras the change of the motor supply from 48 V to 24 V.
- The change follows a recommendation from an industry representative, who considered 48 V excessive for this application.
- The motors' torque-versus-RPM chart also supports the use of 24 V.

**3. Website**

- Dr. Socarras reviewed the changes made to the website, in particular the new navigation at the top of the home page, and found them satisfactory.

**4. Electrical Schematic**

- The team asked for Dr. Socarras's advice on where to place the emergency stop in the electrical schematic.
- Dr. Socarras will follow up with the team.

**5. Future Deliverables**

- Future deliverables will be discussed at next week's meeting.

**6. Project Priorities**

- Dr. Socarras confirmed that the priority is functionality. Provided the work is done safely, shortcuts in presentation, taken to save time or money, are acceptable if they are justified.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Week 6 — 09/28/2026" subtitle="Website navigation, Weekly Task Plan, and documentation schedule">

**Location:** Zoom, 5:00 PM
**Led by:** Dr. Mayra Socarras
**Purpose:** Review the project website, introduce the Weekly Task Plan, and revise the documentation schedule.

**1. Website Navigation**

- Dr. Socarras noted that the website's homepage did not display the site navigation and classified this as a navigation issue requiring correction.
- Resolution: the homepage header now presents the site's sections, with drop-down menus for the proposal and design pages.

**2. Weekly Task Plan**

- Dr. Socarras introduced the Weekly Task Plan, a new document the team will maintain and keep current on the website.
- In a joint planning session, the team will define the work for weeks 6 through 15 as specific, actionable tasks (build, code, test, and document) rather than general statements, assigning an owner to each task.
- At the end of each week, the team will record the status of every task, any changes of direction, and any outstanding blockers.
- The plan will serve as the first point of discussion in each weekly meeting.

**3. Documentation Schedule**

- Dr. Socarras deferred the documentation deliverables by approximately two weeks, allowing the team to concentrate on building the prototype and finalizing the major design decisions before documenting the project in full.

</Accordion>
